items.stem:
The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.
(i) What is the cathode and anode made of in the refining of copper by this process?
(ii) Name the solution used in the above process and write its formula.
(iii) How copper gets refined when electric current is passed in the electrolytic cell?
(iv) You have two beakers 'A' and 'B' containing copper sulphate solution. What would you observe after about 2 hours if you dip a strip of zinc in beaker 'A' and a strip of silver in beaker 'B'? Give reason for your observations in each case.
items.answer:
(i) In the refining of copper the anode is made of impure copper, whereas the cathode is made of a thin strip of pure copper.
(ii) The solution used is acidified copper sulphate, having the chemical formula CuSO₄.
(iii) When electric current is passed through the electrolyte (copper sulphate solution), the metal from the anode dissolves into the solution. An equivalent amount of pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode. The soluble impurities go into the solution and the insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode as anode mud.
(iv) When the zinc strip is dipped in copper sulphate solution (beaker 'A') the blue colour of the solution becomes colourless, because zinc, being more reactive, displaces copper from its salt solution:
CuSO₄(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
When the silver strip is dipped in copper sulphate solution (beaker 'B') no reaction takes place, as silver is less reactive than copper:
CuSO₄(aq) + Ag(s) → No reaction
items.ocr: Formula printed as 'CuSO . $4$' — restored to CuSO₄. Both LaTeX equations rewritten to Unicode; the second lost its arrow and its letters were run together as 'N o r e a c t i o n', restored to 'CuSO₄(aq) + Ag(s) → No reaction'. Exam tag 'OD 2024' printed inside the answer line ('Ans : OD 2024'), moved to the section heading.

items.answer:

items.stem:
A metal M reacts vigorously with water to form a solution S and a gas G. The solution S turns red litmus to blue, whereas gas G, which is lighter than air, burns with a pop sound. Metal M has a low melting point and is used as a coolant in nuclear reactors.
(i) What is metal M?
(ii) What is solution S?
(iii) What is gas G?
items.answer:
(i) The metal M is sodium.
(ii) The solution S is NaOH (sodium hydroxide).
(iii) The gas G, which burns with a pop sound, is hydrogen.
items.ocr: Printed with only three sub-parts; no fourth part is missing from the page.

items.stem:
Refining is the process of purification of metals. One of the important methods of refining is electrolysis. In electrolysis, electrical energy is used to bring about a non-spontaneous redox reaction. This is done by passing an electric current through a liquid containing ions, known as an electrolyte. In contrast to metals, the current in electrolytes is carried by the movement of ions rather than the movement of electrons. The solid conductors inserted into the liquid are called electrodes; the one with a positive charge is called the anode (because it attracts anions) and the one with the negative charge is called the cathode. A diagrammatic representation of electrolysis of copper is shown below.
(i) Name the electrolyte used in refining of copper.
(ii) a. Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻   b. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu
Which of these two reactions occur at cathode and anode?
(iii) What is anode mud?
(iv) Name two metals which can be refined by electrolytic method.
items.answer:
(i) Acidified copper sulphate.
(ii) (a) Reaction a. (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻) occurs at the anode. (b) Reaction b. (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu) occurs at the cathode.
(iii) The impurities which settle at the bottom of the anode as a result of electrolysis are called anode mud.
(iv) Nickel and zinc.
items.ocr: The markdown figure ref sits inside the passage ('A diagrammatic representation of electrolysis of copper is shown below'), so the p35 figure belongs to the question and is attached. The two half-reactions were LaTeX ($\mathrm{Cu}\longrightarrow\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}$ etc.); rewritten to Unicode.

items.stem:
Metals occur in nature in the free as well as in the combined state. The less reactive metals are generally found in the free state. Most of the metals, however, are found in the combined form as minerals. The minerals from which metals can be obtained on a commercial scale are called ores. In other words, the minerals from which metals can be extracted profitably are called ores. Thus, bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) and clay (Al₂O₃·2SiO₂·2H₂O) are minerals of aluminium. However, it is bauxite that is chiefly used to obtain aluminium commercially. So, bauxite, and not clay, is an ore of aluminium.
(i) Which metal occurs in native state?
(ii) Write the name of the sulphide ore.
(iii) What is native of Halide ore?
(iv) Which is the most abundant metal on the earth's crust?
items.ocr: Bauxite formula printed as broken LaTeX '^Al O3 2H Oh' and clay as '(Al_2O_3 . 2SiO_2 . 2H_2O h' — the trailing 'h' is the LaTeX close-bracket artefact; both rewritten to Unicode. Page furniture 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube' and the '## Page 36' marker, which fall between parts (ii) and (iii), were stripped. Part (iii) is printed as 'What is native of Halide ore ?' — kept as printed though the wording is garbled; the answer shows it asks for an example of a halide ore.

items.stem:
The arrangement of metals in a vertical column in the decreasing order of their reactivities is called the reactivity series or activity series of metals. The most reactive metal is at the top position of the reactivity series. The least reactive metal is at the bottom of the reactivity series. Hydrogen, though a non-metal, has been included in the activity series of metals only for comparison. Apart from it, the hydrogen atom also has a tendency to lose its valence electron and form a cation, like the behaviour shown by metals. Thus,
H → H⁺ + e⁻
(i) Which metal can be displaced by copper from its salt solution?
(ii) An element 'X' after reacting with acids liberates hydrogen gas and can displace lead and tin from their salt solutions. Write down the name of metal X.
(iii) Write down the name of the most reactive metal.
(iv) Which metal does not liberate hydrogen gas after reacting with acid?
items.answer:
(i) Silver — copper can displace silver from AgNO₃ because copper is more reactive than silver.
(ii) Nickel.
(iii) Potassium.
(iv) Gold.
items.ocr: 're-activities' printed hyphenated across a line break, joined. LaTeX 'H \longrightarrow H^{+} + e^{-}' rewritten to Unicode. Printed answer (i) reads 'Copper can displace AgNO₃...', i.e. it names the displaced metal indirectly; silver added for clarity.

items.stem:
Activity series — relative reactivities of metals:
Potassium Sodium Calcium Magnesium Aluminium Zinc Iron Lead Hydrogen Copper Silver Gold MercuryMost reactive Reactivity Least
(i) What happens when an iron nail is added to copper sulphate solution? What is the colour change? (ii) Identify the metal which reacts with very dilute nitric acid to evolve hydrogen gas. Name one more metal not given in the above series which reacts in the same way with dilute nitric acid. (iii) Name one important ore of copper with its chemical formula. (iv) Which method is used to extract sodium from molten sodium chloride? (v) Which metal is used in the galvanization of iron?
items.answer:
(i) Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, forming iron(II) sulphate and copper; the colour changes from blue to green.
(ii) Magnesium; and manganese is the other metal that evolves hydrogen with very dilute nitric acid.
(iii) Copper glance, Cu₂S.
(iv) Electrolytic reduction is used for the extraction of sodium.
(v) Zinc.

(i) State one physical property to distinguish between metals and non-metals. (ii) What is the nature of the bond formed when magnesium reacts with chlorine? Write the formula of the compound. (iii) What is common between oxygen and sulphur? (iv) Draw the electron dot structure of O₂ molecule. (v) Name the important ore of aluminium.
items.answer:
(i) Metals are malleable and ductile, while non-metals are brittle.
(ii) An ionic bond is formed by the transfer of two electrons from magnesium to two chlorine atoms; the compound formed is MgCl₂.
(iii) Both have the same number of valence electrons (6) and both belong to the same group (Group 16) of the periodic table.
(iv) The electron dot structure of O₂ shows a double bond — each oxygen contributes two electrons to two shared pairs, O::O (written O=O), with two lone pairs left on each atom.
(v) Bauxite, Al₂O₃·2H₂O.

items.stem:
The earth's crust is the major source of metals. Seawater contains some soluble salts such as sodium chloride, magnesium chloride, etc. The elements or compounds, which occur naturally in the earth's crust are known as minerals. At some places, minerals contain a very high percentage of a particular metal and the metal can be profitably extracted from it. These minerals are called ores.
(i) Name the chief ore of mercury and zinc.
(ii) Write equations for the extraction of copper from its sulphide ore.
(iii) Define the process used to convert carbonate ores into metal oxide.
(iv) Name two metals which exist in their native state.
items.answer:
(i) Mercury — cinnabar, HgS; Zinc — zinc blende, ZnS.
(ii) 2Cu₂O(s) + Cu₂S(s) → 6Cu(s) + SO₂(g)  (on heating)
(iii) The process is called calcination. It is defined as heating the carbonate ore strongly in a limited supply of air to form the metal oxide.
(iv) Silver and gold.

items.stem:
The metals high up in the reactivity series are very reactive. They cannot be obtained from their compounds by heating with carbon. These metals are obtained by electrolytic reduction.
(i) Why can't we reduce oxide of sodium by using carbon?
(ii) Write the steps involved in the extraction of sodium from molten sodium chloride.
(iii) Write one reaction where carbon is used as a reducing agent.
(iv) Why do we use molten sodium chloride and not aqueous sodium chloride for the extraction of sodium?
items.answer:
(i) Carbon cannot reduce sodium oxide to sodium because sodium has more affinity for oxygen than carbon has.
(ii) Molten sodium chloride is electrolysed:
At cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na (reduction)
At anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ (oxidation)
(iii) ZnO + C → Zn + CO
(iv) Electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride liberates H₂ gas at the cathode and not sodium, because hydrogen is lower than sodium in the reactivity series.
items.ocr: 'There metals are obtained' in the printed passage corrected to 'These metals are obtained'. All three LaTeX equations rewritten to Unicode.

items.stem:
Besides using carbon to reduce metal oxides to metals, sometimes displacement reactions can also be used. The highly reactive metals such as sodium, calcium, aluminium, etc., are used as reducing agents.
(i) What happens when manganese dioxide is heated with aluminium powder?
(ii) Identify the substances that are getting oxidised and reduced in the above reaction.
(iii) Complete the following equation: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) →
(iv) What is this reaction of Fe₂O₃ with Al known as?
items.answer:
(i) Aluminium reduces manganese dioxide to manganese, and a large amount of heat is evolved:
3MnO₂(s) + 4Al(s) → 3Mn(l) + 2Al₂O₃(s) + Heat
(ii) Substance oxidised = Al; Substance reduced = MnO₂.
(iii) Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat
(iv) The reaction is known as the thermite reaction.
items.ocr: The answer's LaTeX array scrambled the part labels ('(i', 'i)', '(i' scattered between lines) and printed the Fe₂O₃ + 2Al equation twice; the duplicate line was removed and the parts re-numbered (i)–(iv) against the questions. '3Mn(1)' is OCR for '3Mn(l)' (liquid); restored. The 'Heat' that follows each equation was split onto its own line by the LaTeX array and rejoined. Passage read 'The highly reactive metals oxide as sodium' — 'oxide' is OCR noise for 'such'; corrected.

items.stem:
Alloying is a very good method of improving the properties of metal. Galvanization is a method of protecting steel and iron from rusting.
(i) What is the chemical formula and chemical name of rust?
(ii) Define galvanization.
(iii) Define alloy.
(iv) Name two important alloys containing copper.
items.answer:
(i) Chemical formula: Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. Chemical name: hydrated ferric oxide (hydrated iron(III) oxide).
(ii) Galvanization is a method of protecting steel or iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of zinc.
(iii) An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal and a non-metal.
(iv) Two alloys containing copper are bronze (Cu + Sn) and brass (Cu + Zn).
items.ocr: Rust formula printed as 'F $_{2}O_{3}\cdot xH_{2}$ O' — the 'e' of Fe was dropped; restored to Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. SOURCE DEFECT: the printed answer names rust 'Hydrated formic acid', which is wrong and is OCR/print corruption of 'hydrated ferric oxide'; the correct name is given here and the printed wording is recorded in this note.

items.stem:
According to the octet rule, an atom with 8 electrons in its outermost shell is stable. The noble gases have complete outer electron shells and this makes them very stable. These gases are least reactive as they have a stable electronic configuration. Now, the other elements would also seek stability and hence either transfer the electrons, or gain the electrons, or share the electrons. This rule is very important to understand chemical bonding. The atoms of elements combine to have 8 electrons in their valence shell in order to attain a stable electronic configuration like their nearest noble gases. This rule was proposed by G.N. Lewis and is also known as the Rule of Eight.
(i) What is the number of valence electron in neon gas?
(ii) How many electrons present in helium?
items.answer:
(i) 0 — neon already has a complete octet, so it has no electrons available for bonding (its outermost shell holds 8 electrons, none of which are used in bonding).
(ii) 2 electrons are present in helium.
items.ocr: Printed with only two sub-parts; no further parts appear on the page. The printed answer to (i) is the bare figure '0', i.e. no valence electrons are available for bonding; the explanatory clause is mine and is marked as such here.

(i) Which is the most reactive metal? (ii) What would you observe if Q is added to a solution of CuSO₄? Also, what is the colour change when Q is added to FeSO₄?
